title: Foot Valve

introduction.definition: A foot valve is a non-return valve with a strainer fitted at the bottom end of a pump suction pipe. It opens when the pump draws liquid, and closes when the pump stops so the suction line stays full and the pump stays primed. The strainer keeps solids out.
applications: Centrifugal pumps lifting from sumps, wells and tanks
Fire pumps on open water sources (where permitted)

introduction.summary: A foot valve is a check valve with a strainer fitted at the bottom of a pump suction pipe. It lets liquid flow up to the pump but closes when the pump stops, so the suction line stays full (primed). The strainer keeps debris out of the pump.

foundation: Support the valve and adjoining pipe so the body does not carry pipe weight or thermal loads; heavy valves need their own supports.
alignment: Align flanges face-to-face and bore-to-bore before bolting; never pull pipes into place with the bolts.
Respect the flow-direction arrow on the body.
piping: Keep the foot valve at least ~1–1.5 pipe diameters above the sump floor and well below the minimum level (check ANSI/HI 9.8).
Make the suction pipe airtight and rising to the pump.
commissioning: Check the valve strokes fully and smoothly.
Pressure-test the line (shell test) with the valve partly open; do not use the valve to blind a test above its seat rating.
Record the as-installed position and set points.

routine.task: Check pump stays primed after stops.

symptoms: Pump runs but no flow after restart
causes: Poppet held open by debris, worn seal

video_tutorials.title: Foot Valve — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Foot Valve.
A foot valve is a non-return valve with a strainer fitted at the bottom end of a pump suction pipe.
It opens when the pump draws liquid, and closes when the pump stops so the suction line stays full and the pump stays primed.
The strainer keeps solids out.
Typical applications include centrifugal pumps lifting from sumps, wells and tanks; fire pumps on open water sources (where permitted); irrigation and dewatering; marine bilge suctions.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Valve Body & Seat Ring.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Foot Valve — Operation

script.narration: How the Foot Valve works.
With the pump running, suction lifts the poppet off its seat.
Liquid passes the strainer basket into the valve.
Flow rises through the suction pipe to the pump.
When the pump stops, the spring and the water column close the poppet.
The suction line stays full, so the pump restarts without priming.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Foot Valve — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Foot Valve.
Check pump stays primed after stops.
Lift and clean the strainer.
Replace seat seal and spring.
Watch for loss of prime: pump runs but no flow after restart. Common cause: poppet held open by debris, worn seal.
Watch for cavitation from blocked strainer: noise, low flow. Common cause: clogged basket.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
